back: Temperature = surface temperature − lapse rate × (height in m ÷ 1 000). DALR about 10, SALR about 5-9, ELR average about 6.5 °C per 1 000 m.
The temperature at which air becomes saturated; cooling below it causes condensation.
Stable: ELR less than the SALR (parcel sinks back). Unstable: ELR greater than the DALR (parcel keeps rising). Conditionally unstable: ELR between the two.
Height of condensation level ≈ 125 m × (surface temperature − dew point in °C).
Convection (surface heating), orographic (forced uplift over relief), frontal (warm air over cold air), radiation cooling (dew, fog, frost).
Dry area on the lee of mountains: air descends, warms and dries after losing its moisture on the windward slope.
Warm cloud process: larger droplets fall faster, collide with smaller ones and merge until heavy enough to fall as rain (ZIMSEC detail).
Cold cloud process: ice crystals grow at the expense of supercooled droplets because vapour pressure is lower over ice (ZIMSEC detail).
Layered balls of ice formed in cumulonimbus clouds, where strong up-currents lift ice pellets repeatedly above the freezing level.
A layer in which temperature rises with height; it is very stable and can trap smoke and fog below it.
